case_name: Col. Anil Kak (Retd.) v Municipal Corporation, Indore and Others

statutes.act: Code As A Proceeding Initiated Under Article 227 Of The Constitution

facts: The two petitions arise from the claim for an interim injunction by the petitioner before us in a suit filed by him. The suit was for a permanent injunction restraining the respondents, the defendants in the suit, from interfering with the possession of the suit land allegedly held by the petitioner including the school buildings constructed thereon and not to demolish or take any steps for removal of the constructions.
All that the High Court has done is to treat the petition filed before it under Section 115 of the Code as a proceeding initiated under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.

The trial court, after hearing both sides had confined the interim order of injunction to an extent of 16,000 Sq. ft. and the structures thereon and had declined relief to the plaintiff in respect of the rest of the plaint area, and the constructions allegedly put up by him outside the 16,000 Sq. ft.

An educational institution is functioning in the property in question including the disputed portion and taking note of the fact that from 12.7.2003 the order of stay of demolition granted by this Court has been in operation

There are a number of litigations between the parties, including a suit for specific performance of an agreement to lease filed by the appellant against Respondent No.3 before us apparently in respect of the area outside the 16,000 Sq. ft.
issues: What is the nature of the order passed by the High Court?
Can the respondents challenge the order of the first appellate court under Section 115 of the Code?
Is the order of the trial court justified in confining the interim injunction to an area of 16,000 Sq. ft. and the structures thereon?
petitioner_arguments: The respondents had filed the revision originally and during the pendency of that revision the High Court appears to have taken a view that an order in an appeal arising from a proceeding under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code, could not be challenged under Section 115 of the Code since the order was in the nature of an interlocutory order.
The court could have done it on its own, even without a motion in that behalf by the petitioner.
There is no prima facie case made out by the plaintiff- the appellant before us, for an injunction in respect of the property outside the 16,000 Sq. ft. and the structures thereon
The proposed demolition of structures outside the area of 16,000 Sq. ft. remains stayed.
respondent_arguments: The respondents had filed the revision originally and during the pendency of that revision the High Court appears to have taken a view that an order in an appeal arising from a proceeding under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code, could not be challenged under Section 115 of the Code since the order was in the nature of an interlocutory order.
The respondents are attempting to put up constructions in the disputed property and it is just and necessary to prevent him from doing so
There is no arrears, as claimed by Respondent No.3.
court_reasoning: We see absolutely no ground to interfere with the said order on the grounds raised in this special leave petition.
In our view, the High Court rightly decided to permit the revision petitioners before it, to convert the same as a proceeding under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
The status quo should be maintained in view of the fact that an educational institution is said to be functioning in the property.
We think that this prayer deserves to be granted, especially, in the context of the fact that we are trying to maintain the status quo until the suit is finally disposed of.
We do not think it necessary to decide this controversy.
holding: The order passed by this Court on 12.7.2003 continues to be in operation, meaning thereby that the proposed demolition of structures outside the area of 16,000 Sq. ft. remains stayed.

This appeal is, thus, disposed of by maintaining the order of this Court dated 12.7.2003 until the disposal of the suit and with an injunction against the plaintiff as indicated above and the other directions as contained hereinabove.
